title: Lateral epicondylitis: affected wrist-extensor muscles (wrist extension)
vignette: A 16-year-old girl comes to the office due to several months of left elbow pain. The pain is worse with activity and limits her exercise. She has attempted treatment with over-the-counter ibuprofen and acetaminophen but has had only partial relief. Medical history is notable for seasonal allergies, and current medications include a fluticasone nasal spray. Further evaluation shows that the patient's condition is due to a tendon injury. A long-acting glucocorticoid injection is administered at the most tender spot, which is marked over the lateral epicondyle of the humerus in the image. Which of the following actions is most likely performed by the affected muscle?

clues.text: several months of left elbow pain
clues.note: Chronic activity-related elbow pain from a tendon injury (tendinosis) suggests an overuse epicondylitis.
Epicondylitis is a tendinosis (angiofibroblastic degeneration) at a tendon's origin on the epicondyle, not an acute inflammatory tear.

clues.text: marked over the lateral epicondyle of the humerus
clues.note: Tenderness at the LATERAL epicondyle = lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow), which involves the common EXTENSOR tendon origin - the wrist EXTENSORS.

whatMatters: Pain at the LATERAL epicondyle = lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow). The lateral epicondyle is the origin of the wrist EXTENSORS (extensor carpi radialis brevis, extensor digitorum), so the affected muscle performs WRIST EXTENSION. Answer E. (Medial epicondylitis - golfer's elbow - would involve wrist FLEXORS.)
strategy: Localize by epicondyle: LATERAL = extensors (wrist EXTENSION), MEDIAL = flexors (wrist flexion/pronation). The injection is at the lateral epicondyle, so the affected muscle extends the wrist. Reject wrist flexion (medial epicondyle), and the others (finger adduction = interossei; forearm flexion = biceps/brachialis; shoulder abduction = deltoid/supraspinatus; thumb abduction = abductor pollicis) which don't originate on the lateral epicondyle.

eliminations.label: Finger adduction - palmar interossei (hand)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: adduction of the fingers is done by the palmar interossei, which originate on the metacarpals. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they don't arise from the lateral epicondyle. ✅ Correct if: an ulnar-nerve/interossei question.

eliminations.label: Forearm flexion - biceps/brachialis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: flexing the forearm at the elbow uses biceps brachii, brachialis, brachioradialis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: none originates on the lateral epicondyle (the common extensor tendon does). ✅ Correct if: elbow flexors.

eliminations.label: Shoulder abduction - supraspinatus/deltoid
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: shoulder abduction uses supraspinatus (initial) and deltoid. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: these are shoulder muscles, unrelated to the lateral epicondyle. ✅ Correct if: rotator cuff/deltoid pathology.

eliminations.label: Thumb abduction - abductor pollicis (de Quervain)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: thumb abduction uses abductor pollicis longus/brevis; overuse causes de Quervain tendinopathy at the wrist. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: not a lateral-epicondyle muscle. ✅ Correct if: radial-sided wrist pain (de Quervain).

eliminations.label: Wrist flexion - MEDIAL epicondyle (golfer's elbow)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the wrist FLEXORS (flexor carpi radialis, etc.) originate on the MEDIAL epicondyle; their overuse is medial epicondylitis (golfer's elbow). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this injection is at the LATERAL epicondyle (extensors). ✅ Correct if: medial epicondyle tenderness (golfer's elbow).

reasoning: Chronic activity-related elbow pain from tendon injury at the LATERAL epicondyle = lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow)
The lateral epicondyle is the common EXTENSOR tendon origin (extensor carpi radialis brevis, extensor digitorum)
mechanism: Lateral epicondylitis ('tennis elbow') is an overuse tendinosis at the LATERAL epicondyle of the humerus, the common origin of the wrist EXTENSOR muscles - chiefly the extensor carpi radialis brevis and extensor digitorum. Repetitive wrist EXTENSION (e.g., backhand strokes, repeated gripping/lifting) transmits force through this common extensor tendon, causing angiofibroblastic degeneration (excess fibroblasts and neovascularization, rather than acute inflammation), producing pain and tenderness over the lateral epicondyle and proximal extensor tendons. Thus the affected muscle's action is wrist extension. The mirror-image condition, medial epicondylitis ('golfer's elbow'), affects the wrist FLEXOR/pronator origin on the MEDIAL epicondyle. The other options are performed by muscles that do not originate on the lateral epicondyle: finger adduction (palmar interossei), forearm flexion (biceps/brachialis), shoulder abduction (supraspinatus/deltoid), and thumb abduction (abductor pollicis).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid MSK > lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow) = common extensor tendon (ECRB, extensor digitorum) origin, wrist extension overuse; medial epicondylitis (golfer's elbow) = flexor/pronator origin.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Lateral epicondyle = wrist extensors -> affected muscle extends the wrist.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on lateral vs medial epicondyle, common extensor tendon, extensor carpi radialis brevis, or tendinosis? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Wrist flexion = MEDIAL epicondyle (golfer's elbow); other options (interossei, biceps, deltoid, abductor pollicis) don't arise from the lateral epicondyle.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the photo: the injection/tender spot is at the LATERAL epicondyle (outer elbow), the common extensor origin. Anchor: 'lateral epicondyle = wrist extensors = wrist extension.'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: tennis elbow = lateral epicondyle = extensors (wrist extension); golfer's elbow = medial epicondyle = flexors.

keywords.back: Wrist extension (extensor carpi radialis brevis, extensor digitorum)

keywords.front: Lateral epicondyle is the origin of

keywords.back: de Quervain (abductor pollicis longus / extensor pollicis brevis)

firstAid.detail: MSK: lateral epicondyle = wrist extensor origin (ECRB); wrist extension overuse.
MSK > medial epicondyle = flexors; interossei (fingers), biceps (elbow), deltoid (shoulder).
MSK > overuse angiofibroblastic degeneration, not acute inflammation.

memoryHook: lateraL epicondyle -> Lifting/extending (tennis backhand): the wrist EXTENSORS take the strain, so the sore muscle extends the wrist.
